q: 1. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: Due to the Central Limit Theorem, the total project completion time in critical path network calculations follows a normal distribution.

q: 2. The prime input of material planning is
explain: Material planning primarily depends on forecasting the demand for materials required over the project duration.

q: 3. Actual performance of task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of a task that consumes time and resources.

q: 4. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieved through
explain: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes a project into smaller components to define the interrelationships of functional elements.

q: 5. CPM adopts
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic), CPM is deterministic because it assumes activity durations are known with certainty.

q: 6. Select the correct statement.
options: Activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
The tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
Arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: None of the given statements is correct: arrows are not drawn to scale, the tail represents the start (not finish), and the head represents the finish (not start) of an activity.

q: 7. PERT is an abbreviation for
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Program (Programme) Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 8. A dummy activity
options: had no tail event but had only a head event
had only a head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
had no sequence and can be fitted anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a purely logical connection used to show dependency without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 9. The minimum number of critical path in a net work should be
explain: Every project network must have at least one critical path connecting the start to the end.

q: 10. In CPM, 'Forward Pass' and 'Backward Pass' are used to calculate respectively.
options: earliest expected time and latest allowable time
latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Forward pass calculates Earliest times; Backward pass calculates Latest times.

q: 11. Positive float can occur when it is
explain: A sub-critical activity has a positive float, meaning it has extra time available and does not currently sit on the critical path.

q: 12. Negative float can occur when it is
explain: Negative float occurs in super-critical activities where the time required exceeds the time available, indicating the project is behind schedule.

q: 13. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow a
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are modeled using a unimodal Beta distribution curve.

q: 14. The activity which consumes maximum time is called a
explain: A single activity consuming a lot of time isn't 'called' a specific name in network theory; it is the 'path' that becomes critical.

q: 15. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known as
explain: The point in time marking the start or completion of an activity is called an event (represented by a node/circle).

q: 16. The performance of a specific task in CPM, is known
explain: In CPM, the performance of a specific task is termed an activity.

q: 17. CPM adopts
explain: CPM uses a single fixed time estimate, so it is deterministic.

q: 18. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using the PERT formula $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$: $(1 + 4(3) + 11) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4$ days.

q: 19. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known
explain: Critical ratio scheduling is the specific technique used to set and maintain job priorities based on time remaining versus work remaining.

q: 20. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The weighted average (expected time) in PERT is calculated using the formula $(a + 4m + b) / 6$.

q: 21. The free float affects only
explain: Free float affects preceding activities/successor relationships as per definition[cite: 1].

q: 22. The figure indicates
explain: A node with multiple incoming arrows and one outgoing arrow represents a merge event[cite: 1].

q: 23. The variance will be zero if
explain: Variance is only zero if all data points (durations) are exactly equal to the mean.

q: 24. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for
explain: PERT was developed for and is best suited to large, complex projects with uncertain activity durations.

q: 25. Probability factor is
options: (scheduled time - earliest expected time) / standard deviation
(scheduled time - latest allowable time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - scheduled time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - earliest expected time) / variance
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) is calculated as $Z = (T_s - T_e) / \sigma$, where $T_s$ is scheduled time and $T_e$ is earliest expected time.

q: 26. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve shows how often different values (durations) occur within a data set of completed jobs.

q: 27. Which of the following is a type of bar chart that illustrates a project schedule?
explain: The Gantt Chart is the standard bar-chart form used to illustrate project schedules.

q: 28. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float is defined as the difference between the activity's own latest start time and its earliest start time, without delaying successor activities.

q: 29. The jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Per the answer key, Gantt chart.

q: 30. The total activity slack is equal to
options: late start time - early start time
late finish time - early finish time
latest allowable event occurrence time - early finish time
explain: All three expressions give total float.

q: 31. Which of the following statement is wrong?
options: An activity consumes time and resources whereas an event do not consume time or resources
The performance of a specific task is called an activity
An event is an instantaneous point in time at which an activity begins or ends
explain: All three statements are correct, so none is wrong.

q: 32. In resource leveling the main constraint would be
explain: Resource leveling is performed when resource limits are fixed (constrained), which may lead to an increase in the project duration to stay within those limits.

q: 33. Resource smoothening means
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete revamping of resources to suit the requirement
optimisation and economical utilisation of resources
explain: Smoothening adjusts resources to minimise variation without changing project duration.

q: 34. The time by which the completion of an activity can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is called
explain: That is the definition of free float.

q: 35. Zero float any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float means critical.

q: 36. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called
explain: An event with no outgoing activity is a dangling error.

q: 37. Negative slack occurs
options: when lastest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events sticks to their schedule
explain: Per the answer key, c. Negative slack arises when the schedule is behind, which needs extra resources.

q: 38. A bar chart is drawn for:
explain: A bar chart plots time against activities, with bar length representing each activity's duration.

q: 39. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents:
explain: The critical path represents the minimum time required to complete the entire project.

q: 40. Inputs used during scope planning include all of the following except
explain: Scope planning inputs typically include the project charter, product description, and constraints, but detailed budget/cost analysis is not a direct input to scope planning.

q: 41. A project has three independent critical paths A, B and C. To reduce the project length, we have to shorten
options: The activities of A, B and C
explain: When multiple independent critical paths exist, shortening the project duration requires reducing activities on all of them simultaneously (A, B, and C).

q: 42. CPM requires
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate.
